items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I started studying what they called 'stock arrangements' -- arrangements by Don Redman, Archie Blyer, Arthur Lang, Walter Paul; I guess, Jimmy Dale, Jack Mason ... these are the names I remember

ctx.x: Actually, I started arranging when I was with Charlie Johnson's orchestra at the Small's Paradise. I started arranging by writing saxophone choruses, you know, for 3 saxophones, because that's what we had then, and there were 3 saxophones -- Benny Whittet, Benny Waters and Benny Carter. Three Bennys in the saxophone section.

And I used to write the saxophone choruses, you know, the rhythm section, because they knew all the chord changes and I knew the chord changes, but I didn't know how to do anything else. And I decided I wanted to arrange. I started studying what they called 'stock arrangements' -- arrangements by Don Redman, Archie Blyer, Arthur Lang, Walter Paul; I guess, Jimmy Dale, Jack Mason ... these are the names I remember, and I used to layout the parts on the floor and study them. And I started arranging just like that;…
I was doing it the hard way.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Archie Blyer [phonetic] had a lot to do with that, if the time is right, because we played a few of his arrangements

ctx.x: But I think at this point we’ve talked about how you developed as a saxophonist, to some extent. We should backtrack and figure out how you suddenly in 1928 were already an arranger, and the process by which you learned that craft. First of all, what made you decide that you wanted to arrange? Was there something you weren’t hearing in the music that you felt you wanted to hear?
You mean something I can improve on? No, not at all. [laughter] No, just that I wished that I could just do what I was hearing and do what other people were doing, not

feeling that I could, of necessity, do any better. But gee, I don’t know. I’m not sure, but I think Archie Blyer [phonetic] had a lot to do with that, if the time is right, because we played a few of his arrangements, you know, the stock arrangements, and Arthur Lang [phonetic] and other people, I think, who . . . Bob Herring, Paul Weirich [phonetic]. What other names were there that were doing stock arranging? Jimmy Dale, Jack Mason. I collected their stocks, you know, and I used to spread the parts out on the…
